source: Programme de langues vivantes de premiere et terminale generales et technologiques

quizzes.title: Private and public spaces
quizzes.description: QCM about home, public places, social behaviour and the boundary between private and public life.

questions.prompt: What is a 'public space'?
choices: A place open to many people
A restricted area for staff only
questions.explanation: A public space can be used or accessed by many people.

questions.prompt: Choose the best sentence.
choices: People should to respect shared spaces.
questions.explanation: Use 'should + base verb'.

questions.prompt: A park can be both a place for leisure and a place for civic life.
questions.explanation: Parks can host sport, meetings, celebrations or protests.

questions.prompt: Which phrase expresses a prohibition in a public place?
choices: Smoking is permitted in this area.
This area is open until 8 p.m.
questions.explanation: 'Smoking is not allowed here' clearly expresses a prohibition.

questions.prompt: What does 'privacy' mean?
choices: Control over personal life and information
Being watched in a public space
questions.explanation: Privacy concerns personal life, data and limits.

questions.prompt: Posting a private photo online can make it part of public life.
questions.explanation: Online posts can be copied, shared and seen by others.

questions.prompt: Which connector introduces contrast?
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two ideas.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that gives an opinion.
choices: In my view, cameras can protect people.
Cameras are installed at the station.
The camera is above the entrance.
There are cameras in many public places.
questions.explanation: 'In my view' introduces a personal opinion.

questions.prompt: What is a 'community centre'?
choices: A local place for activities and services
A private home for one family
A workplace closed to the public
An online group with no local space
questions.explanation: Community centres serve local residents.

questions.prompt: Pick the best word: Meeting in public spaces can encourage social ___.
questions.explanation: Social interaction means communication and contact between people.

quizzes.title: Territory, memory and identity
quizzes.description: QCM about places, memory, migration, belonging and cultural identity.

questions.prompt: What does 'belonging' mean?
choices: Feeling connected to a place or group
questions.explanation: Belonging is linked to identity and connection.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: My grandparents moved to this city in 1975.
My grandparents move to this city in 1975.
My grandparents have moved to this city in 1975.
My grandparents were move to this city in 1975.
questions.explanation: Use the past simple with a finished date.

questions.prompt: A monument can keep the memory of an event alive.
questions.explanation: Monuments often commemorate people or events.

questions.prompt: Which word means moving from one place or country to another?
questions.explanation: Migration is movement from one place or country to another.

questions.prompt: Pick the best connector: People moved there ___ they needed work.
questions.explanation: 'Because' gives a reason.

questions.prompt: A territory is only a physical space; it can never have symbolic meaning.
questions.explanation: A territory can also carry memory, identity and power.

questions.prompt: What is 'heritage'?
choices: Cultural elements inherited from the past
questions.explanation: Heritage can include places, stories, objects and traditions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best comparative.
choices: This neighbourhood is more diverse than before.
This neighbourhood is diverser than before.
This neighbourhood is most diverse than before.
questions.explanation: Use 'more diverse than'.

questions.prompt: What does 'roots' mean in an identity context?
questions.explanation: Roots can metaphorically mean origins.

questions.prompt: Which sentence summarizes a balanced view?
choices: A place can change while keeping traces of its past.
A place loses all identity when it changes.
A place can only exist through the past.
A place never changes if people remember it.
questions.explanation: This sentence links change and memory.

quizzes.title: Art, power and protest
quizzes.description: QCM about art as expression, propaganda, protest and social change.

questions.prompt: What is a common purpose of a protest song?
choices: Avoid every social or political message
questions.explanation: Protest songs can criticize and encourage action.

questions.prompt: Choose the passive voice.
choices: The mural was painted by local artists.
The mural painted by local artists was.
Local artists was painted the mural.
questions.explanation: Passive voice: 'was painted by...'.

questions.prompt: Art can be used to support power or to challenge it.
questions.explanation: Art can serve authority, resistance or both.

questions.prompt: What is 'propaganda'?
choices: A public debate between equal voices
An artistic technique with no message
questions.explanation: Propaganda aims to shape beliefs or behaviour.

questions.prompt: Pick the best word: The poster ___ citizens to vote.
questions.explanation: With a singular subject in the present simple, use '-s'.

questions.prompt: A caricature often exaggerates features to make a political point.
questions.explanation: Caricature uses exaggeration and satire.

questions.prompt: Which phrase expresses purpose?
questions.explanation: 'In order to' introduces purpose.

questions.prompt: What does 'censorship' mean?
questions.explanation: Censorship limits what can be said, shown or published.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that analyses an image.
choices: The dark colours suggest fear and tension.
The frame is made of wood.
questions.explanation: This sentence connects visual details and meaning.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'making people aware of a problem'?
questions.explanation: Awareness-raising draws attention to an issue.

quizzes.title: Citizenship and rights
quizzes.description: QCM about civic engagement, rights, duties, media and democratic participation.

questions.prompt: What is a 'citizen'?
choices: A member of a political community with rights and duties
A person who only visits a country
A consumer with no public role
questions.explanation: Citizenship includes rights, duties and participation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best sentence.
choices: Citizens can take part in public debates.
questions.explanation: Use 'can + base verb'.

questions.prompt: Voting is one possible form of democratic participation.
questions.explanation: Voting is a common civic action in democracies.

questions.prompt: What is a 'petition'?
choices: A formal request signed by people
A private message to one friend
questions.explanation: A petition gathers support for a request.

questions.prompt: Pick the best connector: Citizens need information ___ they can make choices.
questions.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose or result.

questions.prompt: A right is exactly the same thing as a duty.
questions.explanation: Rights are protections or freedoms; duties are responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which phrase expresses obligation?
choices: People have to respect the law.
People respect the law if they want.
People might respect the law one day.
questions.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation.

questions.prompt: What does 'freedom of speech' mean?
choices: The right to vote in an election
The duty to respect the law
The right to keep personal data private
questions.explanation: Freedom of speech concerns expression and opinion.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence showing contrast.
choices: Social media can inform people, but it can also spread rumours.
Social media can inform people and share updates.
Social media is used by many citizens.
questions.explanation: 'But' introduces contrast.

questions.prompt: What is 'civic engagement'?
choices: Taking action in public or community life
questions.explanation: Civic engagement means participating in society.

quizzes.title: Diversity and inclusion
quizzes.description: QCM about diversity, inclusion, stereotypes and equal opportunities.

questions.prompt: What does 'inclusion' mean?
choices: Making sure different people can participate
Keeping people apart from public life
Giving access to only one group
questions.explanation: Inclusion means enabling participation and belonging.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Use 'should be + past participle' for this passive form.

questions.prompt: A stereotype is an oversimplified idea about a group.
questions.explanation: Stereotypes reduce people to fixed ideas.

questions.prompt: What does 'equal opportunities' mean?
choices: The same result for every person
A private decision by one person
questions.explanation: Equal opportunities means people should have fair access to chances.

questions.prompt: Pick the best phrase to nuance an argument.
choices: On the one hand... on the other hand...
As a result... as a result...
questions.explanation: This structure balances two sides of an argument.

questions.prompt: Accessibility can concern buildings, websites and school activities.
questions.explanation: Accessibility is not limited to physical spaces.

questions.prompt: Which word means treating someone unfairly because of who they are?
questions.explanation: Discrimination is unfair treatment linked to identity or status.

questions.prompt: Choose the best connector: The policy is useful; ___, it is not enough.
questions.explanation: 'However' introduces contrast.

questions.prompt: What does 'representation' mean in media?
choices: The way people or groups are shown
The legal status of a character
questions.explanation: Representation concerns images, roles and narratives.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most balanced?
choices: Diversity can enrich society if inclusion is actively supported.
Inclusion is unnecessary when society is diverse.
Diversity and inclusion are exactly the same idea.
questions.explanation: This sentence connects diversity with practical inclusion.

quizzes.title: Innovation, progress and ethics
quizzes.description: QCM about scientific progress, technology, benefits, risks and ethical questions.

questions.prompt: What is an 'ethical issue'?
choices: A question about what is right or wrong
A technical detail with no human impact
A faster way to charge a device
A scientific result that needs no debate
questions.explanation: Ethics concerns values, responsibility and moral choices.

questions.prompt: Choose the best sentence.
choices: Technology has changed the way people communicate.
questions.explanation: Use 'has + past participle': has changed.

questions.prompt: Innovation can create new possibilities and new risks.
questions.explanation: Progress often has benefits and limits.

questions.prompt: What does 'breakthrough' mean?
questions.explanation: A breakthrough is a major step forward.

questions.prompt: Pick the best connector: The device is useful; ___, it raises privacy concerns.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' introduces a contrast.

questions.prompt: Artificial intelligence can be discussed through both opportunities and responsibilities.
questions.explanation: AI raises questions about work, bias, privacy and creativity.

questions.prompt: Which expression introduces a consequence?
questions.explanation: 'As a result' introduces a consequence.

questions.prompt: What does 'sustainable technology' suggest?
choices: Technology made only for short-term profit
questions.explanation: Sustainable technology considers long-term environmental impact.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that weighs pros and cons.
choices: While innovation saves time, it may increase dependence on devices.
Innovation saves time and is always positive.
Innovation creates risks and has no benefits.
Devices are popular in many countries.
questions.explanation: 'While' can introduce a concession or contrast.

questions.prompt: What is 'data protection'?
choices: Collecting as much data as possible
questions.explanation: Data protection concerns privacy and security.

quizzes.title: Fiction, reality and media
quizzes.description: QCM about storytelling, news, images, reality, fiction and critical thinking.

questions.prompt: What is 'critical thinking'?
questions.explanation: Critical thinking means questioning, comparing and evaluating information.

questions.prompt: Choose the best sentence.
choices: The article claims that the video is authentic.
The article claim that video authentic.
The article claims authentic is video.
questions.explanation: 'Claims that...' is a useful reporting structure.

questions.prompt: A fictional story can still reveal something about real society.
questions.explanation: Fiction can explore social issues through invented situations.

questions.prompt: What does 'fake news' mean?
choices: A news story from another country
An old article kept in an archive
questions.explanation: Fake news is misleading or false information.

questions.prompt: Pick the best connector: The image looks real; ___, it may have been edited.
questions.explanation: 'However' introduces a warning or contrast.

questions.prompt: A documentary is always completely neutral and never uses a point of view.
questions.explanation: Documentaries can use choices of framing, editing and narration.

questions.prompt: What is a 'source' in media literacy?
choices: The colour used in a headline
The number of words in an article
The device used to read news
questions.explanation: Checking the source helps evaluate reliability.

questions.prompt: Choose the reported speech sentence.
choices: She said that the story was based on real events.
She said the story based on real events.
She said that the story was based in real events.
She told that the story was based on real events.
questions.explanation: Reported speech can use 'said that...' and the correct preposition is 'based on'.

questions.prompt: What does 'bias' mean?
choices: A tendency to present things from one angle
A completely neutral point of view
A source checked by several experts
A fact that can be independently verified
questions.explanation: Bias can influence how information is selected or presented.

questions.prompt: Which question helps verify information?
questions.explanation: Authorship and purpose are key verification questions.

quizzes.title: Identities and exchanges
quizzes.description: QCM about identity, mobility, intercultural exchanges and how contact with others shapes people and societies.

questions.prompt: What does 'identity' refer to in a cultural context?
choices: The way people define themselves and are seen by others
A fixed personality that never changes
questions.explanation: Identity can include culture, language, family, place and personal experience.

questions.prompt: Choose the best sentence.
choices: Studying abroad can change how people see their own culture.
Studying abroad can changes people culture.
questions.explanation: Use 'can + base verb' and clear word order.

questions.prompt: Cultural exchanges can challenge stereotypes.
questions.explanation: Meeting different people can question fixed or oversimplified ideas.

questions.prompt: What is 'intercultural communication'?
choices: Communication between people from different cultural backgrounds
A conversation limited to one family
questions.explanation: Intercultural communication happens across cultural backgrounds.

questions.prompt: Pick the best connector: Meeting new people can be difficult; ___, it can also be enriching.
questions.explanation: 'However' introduces a contrast.

questions.prompt: Identity can be influenced by language, family, place and experiences.
questions.explanation: Identity is shaped by several personal and social factors.

questions.prompt: What does 'mobility' mean in this context?
choices: The movement of people for study, work or life
A fixed place with no movement
questions.explanation: Mobility can refer to people moving between places, countries or cultures.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'unlike'.
choices: Unlike a tourist, an exchange student often lives with local people.
Unlike a tourist because local people.
An exchange student often unlike lives with local people.
A tourist unlike an exchange student because.
questions.explanation: 'Unlike' introduces a comparison based on difference and is followed by a noun group.

questions.prompt: What does 'stereotype' mean?
choices: An oversimplified idea about a group
A balanced description of one person
questions.explanation: A stereotype reduces a group to a simple fixed idea.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most nuanced?
choices: Exchanges can create misunderstandings, but they can also build mutual understanding.
Exchanges always remove every cultural difference.
Identity never changes through contact with others.
questions.explanation: This answer balances possible difficulties and benefits.
